lines: Opening a 2026 Word document (.docx) on a 1992 PowerBook Duo 230.
Written in C89, compiled and linked with MPW on dev2019 (Basilisk II, System 7.6.1), run on the real Duo over AppleBridge.
ZIP → streaming inflate (32 KB window) → WordprocessingML state machine → Unicode → Mac OS Roman → own word-wrapping view.
Tested on the host first: inflate byte-exact on ~450 package members, 3,000 fuzzed files under AddressSanitizer, 0 crashes.

caption: The build machine: Basilisk II with System 7.6.1, MPW and ToolServer. Sources arrive as MacRoman/CR through the shared folder.
First launch after SC → Link → Rez: headings, bullets, table, umlauts all right — but „ shows as a box □.
The byte $E3 is correct MacRoman; Geneva just has no glyph. FMSwapFont's width table (−1 = none) → draw ,, instead.
Own text view (no TextEdit 32 KB limit): Page Down, scroll bar, paragraph spacing.
File ▸ Document Info: 10 KB XML → 5,543 MacRoman characters; 32 spelt with stand-ins, 16 not representable.
File ▸ Save as Text: a TeachText file — real MacRoman bytes, CR line ends, no style markers.

lines: Apps fetched from dev2019 as MacBinary (code lives in the resource fork), sent to the Duo over Ethernet.
The bridge's own screenshot reads noise on the Duo's dock display, so a tiny helper (DuoShot) copies the screen with CopyBits.

caption: The real machine: 68030 / 33 MHz, 8 MB, German System 7, dock display 1152 × 870. The bridge console logs the deployment.
WordReader opens the 2026 .docx: umlauts, «», π Ω, Café recomposed, € → EUR, ½ → 1/2, „ → ,, — and ? where MacRoman has no letter.
Document Info on the Duo: 10 KB of XML inflated and converted to 5,543 MacRoman characters in 2.0 s on a 33 MHz 68030.
Page Down through the longer text: word wrap, paragraph spacing and the scroll bar, all drawn by WordReader itself.
System 7 has no € in Mac OS Roman or in any bitmap font, so WordReader draws it with QuickDraw: an open arc and two bars, as wide as a digit.
Select and copy: drag, Shift-click or double-click, then ⌘C puts plain MacRoman text on the clipboard (€ as EUR), ready to paste into TeachText.

lines: WordReader 1.0: .docx / .docm / .dotx / Word XML on any 68k Mac with System 7 — 33 KB of code, 384 KB minimum memory.
Unicode → Mac OS Roman with stand-ins, recomposed accents, and a font check for glyphs the bitmap fonts lack.
